panels.description: ADR-0036 §8 control plane: what MH did with each forwarding policy MC sent. Counts every RegisterMeeting whose policy MH considered, exactly once, so the sum is a usable denominator. `applied` is health (fresh install, or an idempotent re-assert that correctly performed no swap). `rejected_stale` means reordered or retried delivery on the MC->MH path. `rejected_invalid` means MC sent structurally bad policy - the remedy is upstream in MC's assignment computation. `apply_failed` means MH could not install it (config-apply mailbox full, apply timeout, actor gone, or the aggregate egress-edge bound) and THE PRIOR GENERATION STAYS LIVE; read the `reason` field on the mh.session.policy WARN log to tell those causes apart. `no_generation` IS A ROLLOUT SIGNAL, NOT A STEADY STATE: MC emits policy_generation >= 1 as of story task 13, so the healthy shape is `applied` carrying the traffic and `no_generation` at zero. `no_generation` counting up is expected ONLY while an MC rollout is in progress - a not-yet-upgraded MC pod legitimately still sends 0, so the two series coexist and the mix shifts as pods cycle. That is not an outage. SUSTAINED `no_generation` AFTER THE ROLLOUT COMPLETES means MC failed to compute a generation; the remedy is upstream in MC (check mc_media_policy_pushes_total and MC's mc.register_meeting.trigger logs), not here. A counter materialises no series until first incremented, so an empty panel before the first registration is also correct. Note that mh_grpc_requests_total covers RECEIPT; only this panel covers APPLICATION. See docs/observability/metrics/mh-service.md, and docs/runbooks/mh-incident-response.md Scenario 13 for triage.
panels.title: Forwarding-Policy Applies by Outcome

panels.description: READ THIS PANEL FIRST WHEN TRIAGING NO AUDIO. Connections that attempted to start a media session, one increment each, by terminal outcome. It is the precondition for every other panel in this row: a handler with no started sessions cannot produce a single frame, forwarded or dropped, so this row reading flat-at-zero is ambiguous until you read this panel. started = bound and the three media loops spawned - NOT that media flowed, and NOT a client-side verdict. started climbing while Media Frames Forwarded (ingress) stays flat LOCALISES the fault to at-or-after the spawn and says nothing about which side; this description previously called it a client-side uplink problem and that instruction misdirected three consecutive triage sessions in 2026-09, when the real cause was that nothing in the fleet was sending a datagram at all. Ask the prior question first: if mh_media_frames_dropped_total{reason="transport_receive_dropped"} and {reason="no_media_session"} are ALSO flat, no datagram reached this handler and neither service is implicated yet. declined_no_sender_binding = MC answered with no usable ordinal; the union of MC's 0-answering outcomes, which MH structurally cannot split - meeting_unknown (routing fault), participant_unknown (join race, self-clearing), registry_full (capacity, never self-clears), user_ambiguous (one user with two roster entries; never self-clears, and reconnecting CAUSES it, so the join-race remedy is actively harmful). Read MC's mc_media_sender_binding_responses_total to split them. Discriminate on the RATIO, not the label: a decaying fraction is a join race, flat-and-total is a systematic identity mismatch between what MH names and what MC keys on. declined_sender_binding_out_of_range = MC's allocator RANGE; should read zero forever. declined_sender_binding_conflict = the ordinal is already held by a DIFFERENT participant and MH refused rather than overwrote; should read zero forever, and it is the only decline whose refused binding could have crossed media between participants — CHECK MH's UNBIND PATH FOR THAT MEETING BEFORE PAGING MC. declined_mc_unavailable = MH reached MC or the network and got no usable answer; MH->MC reachability, and it declines only after the whole retry budget. declined_mc_auth_rejected = MH's outbound credential failed - MC refused it, or MH could not build one; MH's OUTBOUND AUTH, NOT MC's health, so do not open MC. Discriminate on the log line "Authorization header parse failed" ON TARGET mh.grpc.mc_client - the target qualifier is load-bearing, because the same message is emitted on mh.grpc.gc_client from the same pod off the same service token, so an unqualified grep fails open. Present on that target = build failure (stay in MH, escalate to auth-controller); absent on that target = refusal (read MC's mc_caller_type_rejected_total). mh_token_refresh_total{status="error"} - what MHTokenRefreshFailures fires on - then mh_token_refresh_failures_total by error_type for why, are context for both routes and separate neither. NO TIMING TELL on this value - the refusal declines immediately and the build failure only after the retry budget, so unlike declined_mc_endpoint_unknown vs declined_mc_unavailable, timing does not identify it. declined_mc_endpoint_unknown = MH had no usable MC endpoint and never reached the network; a REGISTRATION fault, not a reachability one — check what mc_grpc_endpoint the RegisterMeeting for that meeting carried, not MC's health. Every outcome flat while accepted WebTransport connections climb means connections never reach the binding boundary at all — the only pre-boundary terminus left is the JWT gate. NOT a frame drop and never folded into mh_media_frames_dropped_total: this row defines forwarded + dropped = attempts, and a decline is not a frame. Do not build a ratio against accepted connections — see docs/observability/metrics/mh-service.md §mh_media_session_starts_total.
panels.title: Media Session Starts by Outcome

panels.description: Frames MH accepted into the forward path (direction=ingress) and frames the transport accepted for a subscriber (direction=egress). `direction` is PIPELINE-relative (publisher->relay, relay->subscriber), never participant-relative. THIS IS THE DROP-RATE DENOMINATOR — the bytes counter cannot denominate a frame count, so do not delete this panel as redundant; build any drop rate on the ATTEMPTS SUM (forwarded + dropped), never on one addend. READ THIS FIRST IF EVERY MEDIA PANEL IS FLAT: this whole family reads present-and-flat-at-zero both when the handler is idle and when no media session ever started, and the two are byte-identical here. The discriminator is the Media Session Starts by Outcome panel — its outcome value names the cause. (Named by TITLE, deliberately: this sentence previously said "the first panel in this row", which was true only of the then-current gridPos layout, would have been silently falsified by any panel move, and no guard compares a positional reference to the positions it describes.) Full statement: docs/observability/metrics/mh-service.md §Media Forward Path.
panels.title: Media Frames Forwarded by Direction

panels.description: Whether MH is dropping frames, and on which side of the pipeline. THIS PANEL ANSWERS *WHETHER*; the by-reason breakdown that answers *WHY* lives on the "Media Handler - Media Path" dashboard, which splits this counter by reason within each direction. Go there as soon as this panel is non-zero — nothing else on this overview will tell you which condition fired. COUNTED AS increase() RATHER THAN rate() per ADR-0029 Category A: drops are discrete events, and at the deployed 15s scrape cadence a single drop under rate() renders ~0.003/s, which reads identical to healthy on the board an oncall opens first. READ THIS WITH THE FORWARDED PANEL, NEVER ALONE — and note that a flat panel here does not mean forwarding is healthy. Both addends of the attempts sum (forwarded + dropped) are deliberately kept on THIS board so that MHMediaEgressQueueOverflowRate's ratio stays reconstructible where its runbook_url lands a responder. Which tokens should read zero forever, which are expected under load, which mean the remedy is upstream of this handler, and the two structural blind spots (relay-side corruption surfaces only as client-side signature_invalid; quinn evicts silently beneath the egress-overflow counter) are all stated once in docs/observability/metrics/mh-service.md §Media Forward Path. This description points at it rather than restating it. A FLAT PANEL IS AMBIGUOUS AND ALWAYS WILL BE: this family reads present-and-flat-at-zero both when the handler is idle and when no media session ever started, and the two are byte-identical here. Discriminate with the Media Session Starts by Outcome panel first, then with mh_media_frames_dropped_total{reason="transport_receive_dropped"} - flat means no datagram ever arrived, moving means MH received them and never read them.
panels.title: Media Frame Drops by Direction

panels.description: MH's OWN application egress queue depth, in frames — not quinn's send buffer. TREND ONLY: no alert may rest on this panel alone, and it is one process-wide gauge fed by N per-subscriber queues (last writer wins), so a saturated queue can be masked by an idle one. The countable signal is mh_media_frames_dropped_total{reason="egress_queue_overflow"}. Both caveats and the reasoning behind them are stated once in docs/observability/metrics/mh-service.md §Media Forward Path; this description points at it rather than restating it, because the two dashboards had already drifted on the wording. A FLAT PANEL IS AMBIGUOUS AND ALWAYS WILL BE: this family reads present-and-flat-at-zero both when the handler is idle and when no media session ever started, and the two are byte-identical here. Discriminate with Media Session Starts by Outcome first, then with mh_media_frames_dropped_total{reason="transport_receive_dropped"} - flat means no datagram ever arrived, moving means MH received them and never read them. See docs/observability/metrics/mh-service.md §Media Forward Path.
